name: Vietnam
governanceModel: Binding, risk-based national AI law, among the first standalone AI statutes in Southeast Asia
debateTopics: AI-driven job displacement in Vietnam's IT workforce vs. talent shortages
Building a self-reliant 'Make in Vietnam' AI ecosystem vs. dependence on Nvidia and foreign partners
Enforcement capacity for a binding, risk-tiered AI Law taking effect March 2026
overview:
Vietnam has moved faster than most Southeast Asian peers toward binding AI regulation. The Politburo's Resolution No. 57-NQ/TW (signed December 22, 2024) elevated science, technology, innovation and digital transformation to a top national strategic priority, with an explicit goal of ranking among the top three ASEAN countries in AI research and development by 2030; a government Action Program (Resolution 03/NQ-CP, January 9, 2025) followed to implement it. Building on this, the National Assembly adopted Law No. 134/2025/QH15 on Artificial Intelligence on December 10, 2025 — Vietnam's first standalone AI statute — which took effect March 1, 2026. The law, comprising 35 articles across 8 chapters, introduces a three-tier risk classification (high/medium/low) with pre-market approval for high-risk systems in sectors like finance, healthcare and justice, mandatory data-source disclosure and watermarking for generative AI, and penalties of up to VND 2 billion for violations.

On the industrial side, Vietnam signed a cooperation agreement with Nvidia in December 2024 to establish an AI research and development centre and support data-centre buildout (including at state-owned Viettel), part of a reported $250 million Nvidia commitment; Nvidia separately acquired Vingroup's AI healthcare unit VinBrain, and FPT Corporation announced a $200 million AI 'factory' with Nvidia in 2025. Domestic research strength is anchored by VinAI Research (founded 2019, part of Vingroup), described in some rankings as among the world's top 20 AI research organisations, alongside university-based AI institutes such as VNU's AI4SD.

atAGlance.regulatoryApproach: Law No. 134/2025/QH15 on Artificial Intelligence — a binding, three-tier risk-based framework in force since March 1, 2026
atAGlance.latestMajorUpdate: Decree No. 142/2026/ND-CP — the first master implementing decree for the Law on Artificial Intelligence — takes effect May 1, 2026, following the Law itself in force since March 1, 2026
atAGlance.governmentInvolvement: High and centrally directed — Politburo-level Resolution 57 frames AI as a top national strategic priority, translated into a binding national AI law and coordinated ministry/province implementation plans
atAGlance.industrialStrategy: Building a 'Make in Vietnam' domestic AI ecosystem (VinAI, FPT, Viettel) alongside large partnerships with Nvidia on R&D centres and AI 'factories', with a stated target of three major data centres and three AI centres by 2030
atAGlance.internationalPartnerships: December 2024 cooperation agreement with Nvidia on AI R&D and data centres; broader semiconductor-industry ambitions targeting over $100 billion in annual revenue by 2050
atAGlance.primaryPolicyFocus: Implementing the new AI Law's risk-classification and registration requirements, and building out domestic AI compute and talent, appear to be near-term priorities based on recent government statements

currentDirection.summary: Vietnam has moved unusually quickly among Southeast Asian countries from strategic framing (Resolution 57, December 2024) to a binding, risk-tiered AI statute in force since March 2026 — a notably faster and firmer trajectory than most regional peers, which remain at the guideline or draft-bill stage. Implementation capacity and enforcement consistency for the new law's pre-market approval and audit requirements remain to be tested in practice.

recentDevelopments.text: Vietnam features prominently in Nvidia's 'sovereign AI' push: on June 3, 2026 FPT and Viettel are named among a limited group of national partners, with FPT and Nvidia releasing an open, population-scale Vietnamese dataset ('Nemotron-Personas-Vietnam') and Viettel AI building a national legal-sector AI application by fine-tuning Nvidia's Nemotron open models.

The Government issues Decree No. 142/2026/ND-CP (effective May 1, 2026), the first master implementing decree for the Law on Artificial Intelligence — operationalising the three-tier risk regime with a national AI portal and systems database run by the Ministry of Science and Technology, mandatory labelling of AI-generated media, serious-incident reporting within 72 hours, and transition notices for pre-existing systems within 60 days.

Viettel puts into operation Vietnam's first Nvidia DGX B200 supercomputer (eight Blackwell GPUs) at its technical centre in Hoa Lac, Hanoi, describing it as a step toward sovereign, trusted AI capability and the training of Vietnamese-language models.

Vietnam's Law on Digital Technology Industry (No. 71/2025/QH15, passed June 14, 2025) takes effect on January 1, 2026 — described as the world's first dedicated digital-technology-industry law, covering AI, semiconductors, IoT, cloud and digital assets with tax and investment incentives; its AI chapter was subsequently superseded by the standalone Law on Artificial Intelligence that took effect March 1, 2026.

Politburo issues Resolution No. 57-NQ/TW, elevating science, technology, innovation and digital transformation to a top national strategic breakthrough, with a goal of ranking Vietnam among ASEAN's top three countries in AI R&D by 2030.

Vietnam signs a cooperation agreement with Nvidia to establish an AI research and development centre and support AI data-centre development (including with state-owned Viettel), as part of a reported $250 million Nvidia commitment; Nvidia separately acquires Vingroup's AI healthcare unit VinBrain.
Government issues Action Program Resolution No. 03/NQ-CP to implement Resolution 57, followed by ministry- and province-level implementation plans and steering structures.
FPT Corporation and Nvidia announce plans to build a $200 million AI 'factory' using Nvidia GPUs and software.

National Assembly adopts Law No. 134/2025/QH15 on Artificial Intelligence, Vietnam's first standalone AI statute, which takes effect March 1, 2026 with a three-tier risk classification and penalties of up to VND 2 billion for violations.

policyAndRegulation.title: Resolution No. 57-NQ/TW
policyAndRegulation.summary: Politburo resolution (signed December 22, 2024) framing science, technology, innovation and digital transformation as Vietnam's top strategic breakthrough, with an explicit AI R&D leadership target within ASEAN by 2030.

policyAndRegulation.title: Law on Artificial Intelligence (No. 134/2025/QH15)
policyAndRegulation.summary: Vietnam's first standalone AI law, adopted December 10, 2025 and in force since March 1, 2026. Establishes a three-tier risk classification (high/medium/low), pre-market approval and registration for high-risk AI in sectors like finance, healthcare, education, infrastructure and justice, mandatory data-source disclosure and watermarking for generative AI outputs, prohibited uses (e.g. manipulation causing serious harm, exploitation of vulnerable groups), and penalties of up to VND 2 billion for non-compliance.

policyAndRegulation.title: Decree No. 142/2026/ND-CP (implementing the Law on Artificial Intelligence)
policyAndRegulation.summary: Issued April 30, 2026 and in force since May 1, 2026; the first master decree detailing implementation of Law No. 134/2025/QH15. Operationalises the three-tier risk classification, establishes a one-stop national AI portal and a national database of AI systems managed by the Ministry of Science and Technology, mandates labelling of AI-generated media and serious-incident reporting within 72 hours, and required systems already operating before March 1, 2026 to file a transition notice within 60 days.

policyAndRegulation.title: Law on Digital Technology Industry (No. 71/2025/QH15)
policyAndRegulation.summary: Passed June 14, 2025 and in force since January 1, 2026; reported as the world's first dedicated law on the digital technology industry, covering AI, semiconductors, IoT, cloud computing, digital data and digital assets, with tax and investment incentives and a target of building 150,000 digital-tech firms by 2035. Its original AI chapter was superseded by the standalone Law on Artificial Intelligence (No. 134/2025/QH15) that took effect March 1, 2026.

policyAndRegulation.title: Decision No. 1131/QD-TTg (Strategic Technologies List)
policyAndRegulation.summary: Prime Ministerial decision (June 12, 2025) listing AI as a top strategic technology and strategic technology product for national development.

researchEcosystem.summary: Vietnam's most prominent dedicated AI research organisation is VinAI Research, founded in 2019 as part of the Vingroup conglomerate, headquartered in Hanoi with additional offices in Ho Chi Minh City, the US, Europe and Australia; some industry rankings have placed it among the world's top 20 AI research-based organisations, and it draws researchers with prior experience at Google DeepMind, Adobe, Stanford Research Institute and other major labs, though such rankings have not been independently re-verified here. University-based research includes the VNU Institute for Applied Artificial Intelligence in Sustainable Development (VNU-AI4SD), established May 2025 under Vietnam National University, Hanoi, and a 2026 partnership between FPT, VNU Hanoi's Quantum AI & Cyber Security Institute (QACI), and the University of Engineering and Technology focused on AI, quantum computing and cybersecurity talent development.

notableGaps.note: Law No. 134/2025/QH15 took effect only in March 2026; there is not yet a public track record of enforcement actions, high-risk-system approvals, or penalty cases to assess how rigorously the law is being applied.

Compared to some regional peers, Vietnam has fewer independent (non-government-affiliated) think tanks publishing dedicated AI-governance analysis; most authoritative commentary comes from government bodies, law firms, or industry associations rather than independent policy institutes.

No Vietnamese organisation is known to have trained a frontier-scale foundation model from scratch; VinAI and other domestic players focus on applied research and, in some cases, fine-tuning or building on existing model architectures.

debates.topic: AI-driven job displacement in Vietnam's IT workforce vs. talent shortages
debates.summary: Vietnam's roughly one million IT engineers face significant AI-driven role disruption even as employers report acute shortages of AI-skilled talent.
debates.expanded: A mid-2025 Microsoft Vietnam report cited in local reporting estimated that as many as half of Vietnam's IT engineers may need to switch to substantially different roles because of AI, and the Vietnam Software and IT Services Association has reported some companies cutting workforce by as much as 70% after adopting AI tools. At the same time, employer surveys report that a large share of companies struggle to find suitably AI-skilled candidates even while planning to expand headcount, producing what some analysts describe as a 'K-shaped' labour market — rising demand and pay for AI-skilled workers alongside declining demand for others. The scale and permanence of these effects, and how much is genuine displacement versus role transformation, remains actively debated.

debates.topic: Building a self-reliant 'Make in Vietnam' AI ecosystem vs. dependence on Nvidia and foreign partners
debates.summary: Vietnam's stated ambition for a self-reliant domestic AI ecosystem under Resolution 57 coexists with heavy reliance on Nvidia for compute infrastructure, R&D centres and corporate partnerships.
debates.expanded: Official commentary around Resolution 57 has emphasized building a 'self-reliant and sustainable domestic AI ecosystem,' yet the concrete steps taken since December 2024 — the Nvidia AI R&D centre, Nvidia's technical support for Viettel's data centres, Nvidia's acquisition of VinBrain, and FPT's Nvidia-powered AI factory — are all built substantially around a single foreign chip and compute partner. Some domestic commentators frame this as a pragmatic bootstrapping phase toward eventual self-reliance, while others may see it as underscoring how far Vietnam's compute base remains from genuine independence.

debates.topic: Enforcement capacity for a binding, risk-tiered AI Law taking effect March 2026
debates.summary: Vietnam's AI Law introduces a detailed risk-classification and pre-market-approval regime, but questions remain about the government's practical capacity to assess and audit AI systems at the scale the law envisions.
debates.expanded: Law 134/2025/QH15 requires mandatory government assessment and registration for high-risk AI systems in sectors like finance, healthcare, education, infrastructure and justice, alongside sample audits for medium-risk systems and incident-driven monitoring for low-risk ones. Because the law only took effect March 1, 2026, there is not yet a public record of how consistently or rigorously these classification and approval processes are being applied in practice, which is an open question for a regulatory regime this detailed and centrally administered.
